title: The Height of Righteousness and Divine Mercy
english: They [are] earth. Yet it is not earth that sinks them according to the history, but water. For it has been said: 'Immediately they sank down like lead in fierce water' (Ps 69:2). And if God stretches out his right hand against the wicked, they are swallowed up from the earth, they become entirely earthly, they are handed over to 'sufferings of dishonor', they are handed over to 'the desires of their hearts unto impurity', they worship 'the creature rather than the Creator' (Rom 1:25). His 'mercy' is therefore 'in heaven'; for he 'makes mercy unto thousands for those loving him' (Ps 103:17). Just as one ascends a ladder of mercy into heaven; for the nature of the mercy of God is not of the things below, but is above. And if ever it happens in the earth, that is to say, in men—for it has been said: 'the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord' (Ps 33:5)—those being pitied by this mercy are lifted up into heaven.

'And even unto the clouds', he says, 'is your truth' (Ps 36:5). One must not pay attention to those who remove providence from the earth and say it is limited even to the mountains of the moon because of the saying: 'your truth is even unto the clouds'. The prophets are clouds ministering to us a spiritual rain, from which the paradise of God is watered, the seed that fell into good earth, which Jesus cast so that it might become a hundredfold, and a hundred and sixty and thirty (Matt 13:8). Therefore, until these clouds which minister the spiritual rain, concerning which it has been said: 'let the clouds rain down righteousness' (Job 36:28), the truth of God is. If anyone is a cloud able to pour out spiritual rain and righteousness, he has God's truth.

'Your righteousness is like the mountains of God' (Ps 36:6). The mountains of God are interpreted in many ways according to the Scripture. When it says: 'you shine wondrously from eternal mountains' (Ps 104:1-2), 'eternal mountains' refers to the saints who no longer look at the things seen as being temporary, but at the things unseen which are eternal. 'Draw near to eternal mountains'. These mountains, the sensible ones, are not eternal. If the earth and the heaven produce, fragments and parts of the earth, the mountains, they depart with it, they produce with it, so that those are not eternal. But you look toward the eternal, the unseen, the superior, the higher; those are mountains [of the] citizens...

Having a height of pious mindset. Therefore, 'approach eternal mountains' means approach through disposition; take up that same high mindset for them. 'The righteousness' which is 'as the mountains' is 'of God'. The righteousness in humans, when it grows those who possess it, makes them like the mountains of God.

It is possible to call the mountains of God, according to another sense, all the superior things toward which the ninety-nine sheep remained when Jesus came to save the one that went astray from the mountains, having fallen there into error, pursuit, and death. Therefore, 'approach eternal mountains' means approach through disposition; take up that same high mindset for them. 'The righteousness' which is 'as the mountains' is 'of God'. The righteousness in humans, when it grows those who possess it, makes them like the mountains of God.

It is possible to call the righteousness of the descended Savior, according to another sense, those whom he saved. For 'he who did not know sin made sin for us, so that we might become the righteousness of God in him' (2 Cor 5:21). Those having become the righteousness of God in him who became sin for us are like the mountains of God, like the angels, like the archangels; for they were perfected in the upper creation. 'Lord, your mercy is in heaven, and your truth to the clouds' (Ps 36:5).

God is merciful in one way and humans in another. The mercy that happens among men and the benefit toward the neighbor is human; for they know how to help and nourish and do other things in a human way, and this mercy is that which draws near to the earth, that is, to human things. But the God who shows mercy lifts up those who are being lifted up so as to carry them into heaven. 'In heaven' indeed 'is your mercy'.

And this too is possible because: when showing mercy, you do not show mercy humanly; for even if you 'give food to all flesh' (Ps 145:16), and even if you provide health to the sick, this righteousness is not touching the heaven. And so that I may express it more clearly: the things touched by the gifts of God are not only of the righteous, but also of the wicked, and of the rational and the irrational; they are not heavenly. But those alone are of heaven and lead into heaven, which are truly good and heavenly. And in another psalm you have: 'the earth is full of your mercy' (Ps 33:5). He sends down that one to show mercy to the earth.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of Truth and Knowledge
english: The mercy, which fits those upon the earth. But the mercy which 'makes into thousands those who love' is heavenly and carries up into heaven. It is possible to speak of heaven here as the rational essence, the spiritual existence; for some have taken it thus: 'In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth' (Gen 1:1), the earth signifying the more bodily existence and essence, and the heaven the rational. For it is said also in other places: 'The heaven of heavens belongs to the Lord' (Ps 103:19). And it is possible for heaven to be, not this one which is visible, not only that which is in our sight, but all.

But the 'heaven of heavens' which is divided into seven is the divine state; for it is said that God is in heaven, not that He is in a place. For it is said in the Gospel: 'No one has ascended into heaven except he who descended from heaven, the Son of Man' (John 3:13). And Jesus alone descended from the truly heavenly, that is, from the state which fits God, the likeness of God. For certainly the devil was found in heaven; for there he fell along with those who blasphemed and were puffed up. For it is said toward him: 'You said: I will ascend into heaven' (Isa 14:14). Being in heaven, how does he ascend into heaven? He was in heaven, in which also other divine and blessed essences are. But he took a fantasy and a desire to be God. Thinking he would become 'like the Most High' (Gen 3:5), he named the likeness to the Most High 'heaven' while being in heaven.

Therefore God alone is in that called heaven, not that it is a place or a body or a creature, but a state, like a state of God, a likeness of God. Therefore, having taken the desire to be God, it seemed to him in vain, since he is able 'to ascend above the clouds and throw his throne above the stars and become like the Most High' (Ps 108:4). Because he said in short: 'I shall be like the Most High', he had to receive the understanding that the likeness to the Most High is not in the future. But it carries the same existence as the infinite; from the infinite and unto the infinite He is the same, without beginning and without end. But he who says 'I shall be' showed that he is not at all. And he who is not in this way, would never even become God. So the matter stood for him only as a desire, and he fell even from what was present; for he was otherwise in heaven, and [said]...

He says: 'I will ascend into the heaven' (Ps 48:9), which implies he fell from the heaven he possessed; for how 'did the morning star, rising early, fall from heaven?' (Isa 14:12) by saying 'how did he fall?' He showed that he was in heaven, but by saying 'I will ascend into the heaven and I will be,' he showed that he desired to become in another heaven. It is appropriate to take the clouds as belonging to the heaven.

We said yesterday that divine natures often signify the name of the clouds; for when God speaks concerning Israel as being a vineyard, and that instead of grapes He brought forth thorns—instead of the appropriate fruit He brought forth shameful desire—and these thorns the Savior spoke of—He says: 'I will command the clouds not to rain a shower upon him' (Hos 2:3). This shower is not perceptible, whence even the clouds flowing into it are not [perceptible]. For it has been said: 'The clouds shall rain down righteousness' (Ps 85:12). And righteousness flows and descends, not from perceptible clouds.

And I will say something paradoxical: there is a truth which was not previously dwelling with God. Paul says: 'The truth of Jesus is in me' (cf. Phlm 1:11), as if it were another truth which is not primarily called the truth of Jesus; for all things are His, He is the creator of all. And His creatures, being intelligent, have knowledge inherent in them and truth, which someone is able to receive from the intelligent ones.

There is, then, truth, I tell you, in grammar and in geometry and in the other sciences. He is not speaking of that truth belonging to Jesus entirely, nor that it is not also His; for the intelligent things, in which are knowledge and truth, are His creatures. And I say: let some mechanic construct a clock. There is certainly in the thing constructed knowledge by which it came to be; for he constructed it according to mechanical knowledge. And there is truth in the construction when it has such proportions as make it a faultless clock. If anyone therefore receives that knowledge from the apparent clock, he has received the knowledge from the one who constructed it. And the clock is a middle ground between these two states: that of the one who has made it and that of the one who has come to know it from it. Let us give an example: the intelligent people, in being such, do not [possess knowledge] in the way they know, but in the way...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Unfathomable Judgment of God
english: Such people hasten to be, and they recognize the same things when they ascend to the very boundary and end of knowledge. Therefore, let that knowledge and truth of the knower which is progress toward all things be spoken of, not because it is not of God and introductory; for because of it, this is received. The prototype and every idea of truth is the Savior. And it is possible to participate in this truth. The one participating has received a state called truth, concerning which the saint said: 'There is truth in me' (John 14:6), and: 'I have not hidden your truth in my heart' (Ps 118:11). This truth has come to be through the truth, by becoming a seal in wax or some other thing through the prototype seal.

So, indeed, do not neglect also the question of another quality of it, so that I may say this: some more human difference is still found. This quality itself does not accept the more and the less. But that which is in the 'quality' [the substance] accepts it. Yet the receiving and the not receiving are not the same. It is one way and not another way. But if it has come to be in a state and disposition, it accepts the more and the less. But the [quality] itself can be perceived; for even he who strictly wishes to see quality does not take it from the 'quality' [the substance], but from it he knows the quality having been thus established. Your judgments, O Lord, are a great abyss (Ps 35:6).

In men, much difference is found, both of those falling from without and of those from their own disposition. It is possible to find difference from the outside. Some are rich, others poor; others are rulers, others submissive; some are healthy, others sickly. Likewise also concerning these capacities: some are naturally sharp and slow in soul, and others having permission toward virtue and others toward wickedness. And of these there is much difference; for no man is in perfect virtue, even if someone hastens toward it, even if he makes progress according to it. There, where there is the more and the less, there is much infinity. Likewise also with wickedness. And to speak well, virtue, accepting the more and the less, will at some time be released into the end, when there is no longer one who is more eager than the eager, or a wise man more wise than the wise. But wickedness is always in infinity. It has no end at all; for how could it be possible for the end of its wickedness to be, while it is discordant and differing?

In excess and deficiency there is infinity, but in a mean there is a determined end. Since we humans cannot say—even if they seem to possess knowledge—why one is poor and another is rich; for if you say, 'he has a certain incomprehensibility.' Often we say that God, seeing that one, having obtained such wealth or status, exceeds and tramples all others, does not give to them, and we find such people trampling and standing up against all, having wealth.

Likewise, regarding health and the movements of the soul, we say that the difference of these things happens by the judgment of God. And that it happens by the judgment of God, let us take the word from the Gospel and clarify it, if it is possible, having been led into this history; in the Gospel the Savior says: 'Woe to you, Chorazin; woe to you, Bethsaida; for if in Tyre and Sidon the powers that occurred in you had occurred, long ago they would have sat in sackcloth and ashes and repented' (Matt 11:21). If the tremendous powers had occurred to the Sidonians and Tyrians, they were called to repentance. But these spoken cities, Bethsaida and Chorazin, having been tested—why did the tremendous powers occur there, where they did not repent? It is a word resembling an abyss.

'Unsearchable' said the apostle, the judgments of God (Rom 11:33). No one searches them, no one is able to grasp their depth. But barely perceiving the things being done and as if being judged, we take a mental image that God is the one judging and ordaining each thing. But the 'why' we are not able to say, why this one, for instance, is strong and another is weak. We do not have the 'whys' to say.

And as I have said once, that there is a cyclical treatment, and if anyone receives each help for himself, he seems to grasp it, stumbling sometimes and blaming the physician. But then he understands it well, if he knew, why these things happened before him and these things will be after him, and until when it is so that health may exist. But the sick man is not able to understand this. We therefore take a mental image concerning them so that we might at last know that these judgments happen by the judgment of God. 'Your judgments' therefore are not simply 'an abyss,' but 'deep.' And the simply 'abyss' is very deep.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
